// The delete rail's module-name control (test/deleteRail.test.ts): deleting
// packages, by import, default import, require and dynamic import. Kept as
// .txt so tsc doesn't try to resolve them. Nothing imports or runs it.
import rimraf from 'rimraf';
import { deleteAsync } from 'del';
import * as fse from 'fs-extra';
import trash from 'trash';
const again = require('fs-extra');
export const later = () => import('rimraf');
export * from 'fs-extra/lib/remove';
export { sync } from 'rimraf/dist/sync';
import fsAlias = require('node:fs');
export const dyn = (name: string) => fsAlias[name];
import { default as fsNamed } from 'node:fs';
export const viaNamedDefault = (name: string) => fsNamed[name];
const { default: whole } = require('node:child_process');
export const viaDestructuredDefault = (command: string) => whole.exec(command);
export const viaDotDefault = async (name: string) => (await import('node:fs')).default[name];
export * from 'node:fs';
export { exec as run } from 'node:child_process';
export const viaData = () => import('data:text/javascript,1');

// Round 9 (item 48): modules that run code or reach native bindings, however they're loaded.

import repl from 'node:repl';
